newsitem.title: TURKEY: Union/Turkish airline THY pay talks fail.
newsitem.headline: Union/Turkish airline THY pay talks fail.

text.p: The opening round of talks between Turkey's state airline Turk Hava Yollari (THY) and the trade union Hava-Is ended without agreement on Thursday, Hava-Is officials said.
"A memorandum of disagreement covering 26 articles was signed," said Atilay Aycin, head of the trade union.
"Now an official mediator will be appointed within 21 days from today," he told Reuters.

Hava-Is and THY, which has more than 7,000 workers who are members of the trade union, have been in talks since December to renew the collective bargaining agreement for two years from the beginning 1997.
Aycin said the union demanded a pay rise of 170 percent for the first six month of this year, and later rises in line with the official inflation rate for the remaining period.

But the airline offered 40 percent for the first six months and a 25 percent rise for each of the three remaining six-month periods. The year-on-year consumer inflation rate was 79.8 percent in January.

Aycin said the union would declare a strike if the official mediator failed to find a common ground between the union and THY. "After that we will have 60 days to go on a strike unless we reach an agreement in bilateral talks during this period."
